sections.title: リーディング・ライティング

items.q:
A: Could you (　) me how to use this machine?
B: Sure. Just press the green button.
items.ex: show 人 how to ～ で「人に～の仕方を見せて教える」。

items.q: The concert was (　) because the singer was sick.
items.ex: call off で「中止する」(cancel と同じ)。

items.q: Our teacher (　) us to read at least one book a month.
items.ex: encourage 人 to ～ で「人に～するよう勧める・はげます」。suggest や hope はこの形をとりません。

items.q: I'll lend you this book (　) you promise to return it next week.
items.ex: if=もし～なら。「来週返すと約束するなら貸すよ」。

items.q: It has been raining (　) last night.
items.ex: since ～ で「～から(今までずっと)」。現在完了進行形と一緒に使います。

items.q: Mr. Kato is (　) for his kindness, so everyone likes him.
items.ex: be known for ～ で「～で知られている」。

items.q: Please (　) your phone when the movie starts.
items.ex: turn off で「(電源を)切る」。

items.q:
A: Have you decided (　) to go for summer vacation?
B: Not yet.
items.ex: where to go で「どこへ行くか」。

items.q: The company is looking for people who can speak more than one (　).
items.ex: language=言語。「2つ以上の言語を話せる人」。

items.q: We need to leave now. (　), we'll miss the last bus.
items.ex: otherwise=そうしないと。

items.q: She was so (　) that she fell asleep on the train.
items.ex: 人が「疲れている」は tired。

items.q: The new library has more than 50,000 books, so it is (　) larger than the old one.
items.ex: 比較級を強めるのは much(ずっと)。very は使えません。

items.q: My brother is good at (　) things, so he often fixes our computer.
items.ex: repair=修理する。fixes(直す)がヒントです。

items.q: I don't know the (　) to this question. Can you help me?
items.ex: the answer to the question で「その質問の答え」。

items.q:
A: Shall we take a taxi?
B: No, the station is (　) walking distance.
items.ex: within walking distance で「歩いて行ける距離に」。

items.q:
A: I'm going to the supermarket. (　)
B: Yes, could you buy some eggs?
items.ex: B が「卵を買ってきて」とたのんでいるので、何か必要か聞いています。

items.q:
A: How was your job interview yesterday?
B: (　) I'll find out next week.
A: Good luck!
items.ex: 結果は来週わかるので、「うまくいったと思う」。

items.q:
A: Excuse me. I think you gave me the wrong change.
B: (　)
A: It should be 300 yen, but you gave me 200 yen.
o: Oh, I'm sorry. How much did I give you?
items.ex: A がいくら渡されたかを答えているので、金額をたずねています。

items.q:
A: Why don't we go to the beach this weekend?
B: (　)
A: Then how about going to the aquarium instead?
o: It's going to rain this weekend.
items.ex: 「じゃあかわりに水族館は?」と続くので、雨の予報が入ります。

items.q:
A: I can't open this jar.
B: (　)
A: Thanks. You're so strong.
items.ex: 「ありがとう、力持ちだね」と続くので、「やってみるよ」。

blocks.title: Kindergartens in the Forest
blocks.body:
In some countries, such as Germany and Denmark, there are kindergartens where children spend most of the day outside in the forest. These "forest kindergartens" do not have classrooms. Even when it rains or snows, the children play among the trees, build things with sticks, and watch insects and birds.
Some parents worry that it might be dangerous. However, teachers say that the children ( 21 ). They learn which branches are strong enough to climb on and how to walk carefully on wet ground.
Studies have also shown that children who spend a lot of time outside are often healthier and more creative. ( 22 ), forest kindergartens have become popular in other countries, including Japan.

o: learn to understand risks by themselves
are not allowed to climb trees
spend most of the time reading
qs.ex: 直後に「どの枝なら登れるか、ぬれた地面の歩き方を学ぶ」とあるので、「危険を自分で判断できるようになる」。
健康や創造性によいという利点を受けて「こうした利点から」ほかの国でも人気に、とつながります。

blocks.label: [A]
blocks.body:
From: Emily Carter
To: Kaito Ono
Date: March 2
Subject: Your homestay

Hi Kaito,
We're so happy that you'll stay with our family this summer! My parents and I will meet you at Vancouver Airport on July 20. Our house is about forty minutes from the airport by car. You'll have your own room on the second floor, and you can see the mountains from the window.
During your stay, you'll go to an English school in the city on weekdays. On weekends, we're planning to go hiking and take a boat trip to see whales. My little brother, Noah, is very excited, too. He loves Japanese anime, and he wants you to teach him some Japanese words.
By the way, are there any foods that you can't eat? Please let us know before you come. Also, the evenings can be cold here even in summer, so please bring a jacket.
See you soon,
Emily

qs.q: How will Kaito get to Emily's house from the airport?
qs.ex: 家族が空港に迎えに来て、家までは車で40分です。

qs.q: What does Noah want Kaito to do?
qs.ex: he wants you to teach him some Japanese words とあります。

qs.q: Why should Kaito bring a jacket?
o: It may be cold in the evenings.
qs.ex: the evenings can be cold here even in summer とあります。

blocks.label: [B]
blocks.title: A Bank for Seeds
blocks.body:
On a cold island in the Arctic Ocean, there is a special building that some people call the "Doomsday Vault." Its real name is the Svalbard Global Seed Vault. It was opened by the government of Norway in 2008, and it stores seeds of crops such as rice, wheat, and beans from many countries around the world.
Why are these seeds kept so far away? Many countries have seed banks of their own. However, wars, natural disasters, or even simple accidents can destroy them. The vault in Svalbard is a backup. It was built deep inside a mountain, and the temperature inside is kept at about minus 18 degrees Celsius, so the seeds can stay alive for a very long time.
In 2015, the vault was used for an important purpose for the first time. Because of the war in Syria, scientists there could no longer use their seed bank in the city of Aleppo. They took out some of the seeds that they had sent to Svalbard and started growing them again in other countries.
Today, more than a million samples of seeds are kept in the vault. Scientists hope that it will help people grow enough food in the future, even if the climate changes.

qs.q: What is the Svalbard Global Seed Vault?
o: A place that stores seeds from around the world.
A farm that grows rice and wheat.
A laboratory that makes new crops.
qs.ex: 世界中の作物の種を保管する施設です。

qs.q: Why can seeds stay alive in the vault for a long time?
o: The building is close to the sea.
They are kept in plastic bottles.
qs.ex: 中はマイナス18度ほどに保たれているからです。

o: The vault was damaged by a disaster.
Seeds were taken out of the vault for the first time.
qs.ex: シリアの科学者が、預けていた種を初めて取り出しました。

qs.q: Which of the following statements is true?
o: The vault stores only seeds from Norway.
The vault was built in a warm place.
Many countries have their own seed banks.
Scientists in Syria grew the seeds in Svalbard.
qs.ex: Many countries have seed banks of their own. とあります。

parts.prompt:
あなたは、外国人の知り合い(Taylor)から、Eメールで質問を受け取りました。この質問にわかりやすく答える返信メールを英文で書きなさい。
あなたが書く返信メールの中で、Taylorのメールの下線部(cooking lessons)について、あなたがより理解を深めるために、下線部の特徴を問う具体的な質問を2つしなさい。
返信は「Hi, Taylor! Thank you for your e-mail.」で始まり「Best wishes,」で終わります(この部分は書かなくてよい)。
parts.body:
Hi!
Guess what? I started taking [cooking lessons] last month. It's a lot of fun, and I can make a few dishes now. My teacher says cooking is a skill that everyone should learn. Do you think young people should learn how to cook?
Your friend,
Taylor
rules: 語数の目安は40語〜50語です。
Taylorの質問に答えること、下線部(cooking lessons)について質問を2つすることの両方が必要です。
parts.model: Yes, I think so. If young people can cook, they can eat healthy food when they live alone. By the way, I want to know more about your cooking lessons. Where do you take them? And what was the first dish you made?
checks: Taylorの質問(若い人は料理を学ぶべきか)に答えている
答えの理由も書いている
cooking lessons について具体的な質問を2つしている(Where…? What was the first dish…? など)
語数が40〜50語になっている
スペルや文法のミスがない
parts.title: ライティング(Eメール)

parts.prompt:
あなたは、外国人の知り合いから以下のQUESTIONをされました。QUESTIONについて、あなたの意見とその理由を2つ英文で書きなさい。

QUESTION
Do you think it is a good idea for families to eat dinner together every day?
rules: 語数の目安は50語〜60語です。
理由は2つ書きましょう。
QUESTIONに答えていない場合や、内容がQUESTIONからずれている場合は、0点と採点されることがあります。
parts.model: I think it is a good idea for families to eat dinner together every day. I have two reasons. First, family members can talk about what happened during the day. Second, parents can make sure that their children eat healthy meals. For these reasons, I strongly agree with this idea.
checks: 最初に賛成か反対かをはっきり書いている
First, Second, For these reasons などで構成がわかる
語数が50〜60語になっている
スペルや文法のミスがない
parts.title: ライティング(英作文)

lines: Excuse me, is this seat free?
Do you mind if I open the window?
items.ex: Do you mind if ～?(～してもかまいませんか)には Not at all.(どうぞ)。

lines: Mom, I got a C on my math test.
items.ex: 勉強が足りなかった→「次はもっと勉強しなさい」。

lines: Hi. I left my umbrella on the number 8 bus this morning.
items.ex: 色を聞かれているので色で答えます。

lines: Are you going to try out for the school play?
I want to, but I'm too shy.
You should try. You're a great singer.
items.ex: はげまされて「ありがとう。やってみようかな」。

lines: Welcome to Green Gym. How can I help you?
I'd like to know about your membership plans.
Would you like to come on weekdays or weekends?
items.ex: 平日か週末かを聞かれて「主に週末」。

lines: Did you hear that the new café opened near the station?
items.ex: How was it?(どうだった?)に感想で答えます。

lines: Excuse me. Where can I find books about dinosaurs?
o: No, it's on the third floor.
items.ex: この階かどうか聞かれて「いいえ、3階です」。

lines: Hi, Jack. Are you ready for your trip to Australia?
Almost. I just need to buy a new suitcase.
You can borrow mine if you want.
items.ex: スーツケースを貸すと言われて喜んでいます。

lines: Dad, can you help me with my science project?
How plants grow in the dark.
items.ex: 「おもしろいね。今夜始めよう」と手伝いを引き受けています。

lines: Excuse me. How long does it take to get to the airport?
When does the next train leave?
items.ex: When(いつ)なので時間で答えます。

lines: Hi, Kevin. Do you want to go to the movies on Saturday?
I'd love to, but I have a basketball game that day.
items.q: When will they go to the movies?
items.ex: 土曜は試合なので、日曜日に行きます。

lines: Excuse me. Do you have this jacket in black?
I'm sorry, we only have it in brown and gray.
Can you order a black one?
Yes, but it will take about two weeks.
items.q: What does the woman say about the black jacket?
o: It will take about two weeks to get.
It is on the second floor.
items.ex: 取り寄せに約2週間かかると言っています。

lines: Dad, can I go to Lucy's birthday party on Saturday?
Sure. How will you get there?
Lucy's mother will pick me up.
OK. Call me when you want to come home.
items.q: How will the girl get to the party?
o: Lucy's mother will pick her up.
items.ex: ルーシーのお母さんが迎えに来てくれます。

lines: Hello, this is Jim from Sunrise Travel. Your tickets to Paris are ready.
Great. Can I pick them up tomorrow?
Sure. We're open from ten to six.
items.q: What will the woman do tomorrow?
items.ex: 明日のお昼ごろチケットを受け取りに行きます。

lines: I want to get a part-time job this summer.
Why don't you work at the swimming pool? They're looking for people.
But I'm not a good swimmer.
They need people to sell tickets, too.
items.q: What does the girl suggest?
items.ex: 泳ぎが得意でなくても、チケット売りの仕事があると勧めています。

lines: Excuse me. My room is very cold. I think the heater is broken.
I'm very sorry. I'll send someone to check it.
Thank you. Could you also bring an extra blanket?
items.q: What will the man do?
o: Give the woman a new room.
Send someone to check the heater.
items.ex: I'll send someone to check it. と言っています。

lines: I'm worried about my speech tomorrow.
Yes, but I always forget some parts.
Why don't you write the main points on a small card?
items.q: What does the boy suggest?
o: Writing the main points on a card.
items.ex: 要点を小さなカードに書くよう勧めています。

lines: Honey, the car is making a strange noise.
Again? We just had it checked last month.
I'll take it to the garage tomorrow.
Then I'll take the bus to work.
items.q: How will the woman go to work tomorrow?
items.ex: 車は修理に出すので、バスで行きます。

lines: Mom, there's no milk for my cereal.
Sorry, I forgot to buy it. Can you eat toast instead?
items.q: What will the boy eat for breakfast?
items.ex: 牛乳がないので、ジャムをつけたトーストを食べます。

lines: Excuse me. Is the art museum open on Mondays?
No, it's closed on Mondays. It's open from Tuesday to Sunday.
Oh, I see. What time does it open?
items.q: What does the man say about the art museum?
items.ex: it's closed on Mondays と言っています。開館は9時半です。

lines: Sophie wanted to make friends at her new school, so she joined the art club. At first, she was too shy to talk, but the other members were friendly. Now she has many friends, and they often draw together after school.
items.q: Why did Sophie join the art club?
o: She wanted to win a prize.
items.ex: 新しい学校で友達を作りたかったからです。

lines: Attention, shoppers. Our store will close at six today instead of nine because of a power check. We are sorry for the trouble. Please finish your shopping before six.
items.q: Why will the store close early today?
items.ex: because of a power check(電気設備の点検のため)とあります。

lines: Koalas sleep for up to twenty hours a day. This is because their main food, eucalyptus leaves, does not give them much energy. Koalas need to rest a lot to save energy.
items.q: Why do koalas sleep so much?
o: They are afraid of other animals.
Their food does not give them much energy.
items.ex: ユーカリの葉からはあまりエネルギーがとれないからです。

lines: Last month, Ryota's grandmother started using a smartphone. At first, she could only make phone calls. Ryota taught her how to send pictures, and now she sends him photos of her garden every week.
items.q: What does Ryota's grandmother do every week now?
o: She sends Ryota photos of her garden.
items.ex: now she sends him photos of her garden every week とあります。

lines: Thank you for flying with Sky Wing Airlines. We will be landing at Narita Airport in about thirty minutes. Please return to your seats and fasten your seat belts. Do not use the restrooms at this time.
items.q: What should passengers do now?
items.ex: 席にもどってシートベルトを締めるよう案内しています。

lines: Mr. Wilson runs a small bakery. Every morning, he gets up at four to bake bread. Recently, more customers have asked for bread without sugar, so he started making a new kind of healthy bread.
items.q: Why did Mr. Wilson start making a new kind of bread?
o: He wanted to win a contest.
Customers asked for bread without sugar.
items.ex: 砂糖なしのパンを求める客が増えたからです。

lines: Every year, Mika's town holds a festival in August. This year, Mika helped make lanterns for the festival. She painted pictures of fish and flowers on them. Many visitors took photos of her lanterns.
items.q: What did Mika do for the festival this year?
items.ex: Mika helped make lanterns for the festival とあります。

lines: Good morning, students. Because of the heavy rain, today's soccer practice will be held in the gym instead of on the field. Please bring your indoor shoes.
items.q: What should the students bring?
items.ex: Please bring your indoor shoes. とあります。

lines: Tom wanted to save money to buy a new camera. He stopped buying snacks after school and put the money in a box every day. After four months, he had enough money to buy the camera he wanted.
items.q: How did Tom save money?
o: He got money from his parents.
items.ex: 放課後のおやつを買うのをやめてお金をためました。

lines: Penguins cannot fly, but they are excellent swimmers. Some penguins can swim at about thirty kilometers per hour. They use their wings like fins to move through the water.
items.q: How do penguins use their wings?
items.ex: They use their wings like fins to move through the water. とあります。
